Inherited microcytic hypochromic anemia with iron overload; hepatic iron deposition alone does not establish common liver dysfunction across the umbrella.

Glomerulosclerosis/nephrotic renal dysfunction and developmental impairment with variable epilepsy define the syndrome; other structural findings lack adequate frequency.
Pythium infection directly invades arteries in roughly 50-60% and the eye in roughly 30-40% of reported human cases; cutaneous disease is less common.
Glycosylation disorder with developmental impairment in 7/7; hearing loss and neurogenic bladder each occur in 2/7, below threshold; hepatic findings are occasional.
Mitochondrial spastic ataxia; neurogenic bladder causes urinary dysfunction in 13/23, and scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Hearing loss is uncommon (3/23).
Primary biliary cholangitis is autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts; this genetic subtype does not establish additional common organ damage.
Defining alopecia/keratoderma, acro-osteolysis and destructive periodontal disease with tooth loss; ventricular tachycardia is reported without established common frequency.
Leukocyte inclusion bodies, anemia and leukemia establish blood/marrow disease; cardiac and lymphatic findings lack evidence of common involvement.
Genetically defined acute myeloid leukemia involving marrow and myeloid blood cells.
Renal cystic dysplasia, MODY5 and neurodevelopmental disorders are defining syndrome domains; other organ abnormalities are occasional.
Idiopathic granulomatous inflammation directly damages skeletal muscle and represents an immune-mediated inflammatory myopathy.
Persistent intrahepatic portosystemic vessel diverts portal blood and impairs hepatic clearance; encephalopathy is variable and lacks a reliable common frequency.
Congenital skeletal malformation of the hands and feet; no additional common organ disease is established.
